subject: Commit tier guardrails and rate protections for Acme
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <j.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: commit tiers + rate protections

John —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attached is a concise term sheet (redwood_commit_term_sheet_v2.pdf) that maps the commit tiers we discussed to per-token effective rates for our Hosted API. High level:

- 12-month commit options: $50k/mo (~300M tokens/mo), $100k/mo (~650M tokens/mo), $200k/mo (~1.5B tokens/mo).
- Baseline per-token rates, step discounts at each tier, and a quarterly true-up for usage variance.

On rate protections, you asked for clarity around price locks, MFN, and CPI caps. We propose the following starting point (details in the attached):

1) Price lock: 9 months on per-token list rates from contract effective date.
2) CPI cap: annual increase capped at 3% (we can discuss jurisdiction+index if you need CPI-U vs CPI-W).
3) MFN: mutual‑for‑neighbor limited to customers with similar commit size (>=75% of your commit) and same region (US). MFN does not apply to promotional or time-limited pilot pricing.

Why these limits? They let us commit to predictable unit economics for you while protecting our ability to run promotional programs and price for very different scale customers. That said, we are open to negotiating stronger protections if you increase the committed volume or extend the initial term.

Next steps I suggest: you review the term sheet and tell me the one or two items you most want tightened. If you can share procurement timelines we’ll prioritize legal redlines.

Attaching: redwood_commit_term_sheet_v2.pdf and a short summary of how the quarterly true-up works.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

---
Attachment: redwood_commit_term_sheet_v2.pdf (term sheet, 3 pages)
From: John Doe <j.doe@acme.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Corp Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: commit tiers + rate protections

Rachel —

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the term sheet. A few quick responses from procurement and finance: they like the tier structure but want firmer protections on price movement and MFN. Specific asks: 

- Price lock: 12 months minimum (your 9 months feels short).
- CPI cap: as low as possible — finance prefers 1.5% but understands market forces; asking if you can do 2% with a cap on any model-revision-driven bumps.
- MFN: procurement wants an unconditional MFN for ANY publicly available published per-token rate for equivalent or lower tiers — they are concerned promotional carveouts will be used to undercut us.

Also, legal wants to see a redline showing MFN definitions and any region/scale carveouts. I attached our internal requirements for reference (acme_requirements_summary.pdf).

If you can get back to us by EOD Wednesday that would keep us on track for procurement review next week.

—John
John Doe
Director of Product Operations | Acme Corp
j.doe@acme.com

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Proposal: commit tiers + rate protections — Acme asks

Looping you both in — after John’s reply procurement is pressing for: 12 month lock, unconditional MFN, and CPI <=2%. Legal asked for a redline on MFN definitions.

My recommended negotiation posture:

1) Price lock: increase our offer to a 9 -> 12 month lock if Acme moves to the $100k/mo or $200k/mo tier OR accepts a 15-month auto-renew that includes a price review. If they stick to $50k/mo we hold at 9 months.

2) CPI cap: meet at 2.5% (compromise). If they push for 2% we ask for a 10% increase in committed volume or a one-time onboarding fee credit removal.

3) MFN: we can agree to MFN but narrowly define it: applies only to publicly posted list rates for identical product/configuration for customers in the same region and >=75% commit size. Explicit carveouts: promotional pilots, partner marketplace promos, temporary trial rates, and negotiated enterprise carveouts for strategic deals. We should include a 90-day sunset on post-publication price changes for MFN claims.

4) Concessions: offer a 3-month burst credit (10% of first-quarter committed spend) if they sign by 3/31. That gives sales leverage and limits long-term revenue impact.

Legal ask: I attached a working redline of the MFN clause (redline_commit_terms.docx). Please review and flag any legal non-starters.

Thoughts? If you approve I’ll send an updated redline and the mutual action plan with dates for procurement, security review, and signature.

Thanks,
Rachel

---
Attachment: redline_commit_terms.docx (redline of MFN and price-lock clauses)
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposal: commit tiers + rate protections — Acme asks

Rachel —

Agree with your posture. Two small edits:
- Make the MFN carveouts explicit in the first paragraph and include the 90-day post-publication window.
- For CPI, we can accept 2.5% but add a clause that model-architecture changes that materially increase inference cost are excluded from the cap, with 60-day notice.

Approve sending updated redline + MAP. Keep me on copy when you send to John.

—Sean
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Proposal: commit tiers + rate protections

Rachel / Sean —

Thanks for the quick internal alignment and the updated redline. Procurement reviewed your carveouts and the 90-day window — that seems acceptable as long as MFN covers any publicly posted list rates for equivalent tiers. Finance will accept 2.5% CPI cap with the model-change carveout you described, provided changes are documented with cost impact analysis.

We are willing to move to the $100k/mo commit tier (ACME-2027-EXP-0041) if you:
- Lock list rates for 12 months (you agreed to 12 months for $100k tier).
- Keep the MFN definition as redlined (public list rates, >=75% commit, same region).
- Include the 3-month 10% burst credit as a signing incentive.

Legal says share the final contract redline and we’ll circulate to signatories. Procurement also requested a short mutual action plan with target dates for security questionnaire, legal redline, and DocuSign routing.

If you send the updated doc I’ll get our legal team to review and aim to finish signs by 3/31.

—John
